name: Matrix-isolation FTIR spectroscopy of a sublimed heterocycle in solid argon at 15 K with broadband UV photolysis
plain_name: Trap single molecules in frozen argon and study them with infrared light
description: A heterocyclic compound is sublimed and co-deposited with a large excess of argon onto a CsI window held at 15 K inside a closed-cycle helium cryostat evacuated to about 3.5e-5 mbar; mid-IR spectra (4000-400 cm-1) are recorded on the isolated monomers and followed through broadband UV irradiation from a 500 W Hg(Xe) lamp. This is the standard matrix-isolation route to conformers, photoproducts and reactive intermediates in chemistry.
keywords: Trap single molecules in frozen argon and study them with infrared light

sources.citation: İsa Sıdır, Susy Lopes, Rui Fausto, A. J. Lopes Jesus, Molecular Structure, Matrix-Isolation IR Spectrum and UV-Induced Transformations of 2-Amino-5-(4-Methoxyphenyl)-1,3,4-Oxadiazole, Molecules 30(16):3444 (2025), doi:10.3390/molecules30163444

Daria Bumażnik, Magdalena Sałdyka, UV-Induced Photodegradation of 2-Aminothiazole-4-Carboxylic Acid: Identification of New Carbodiimide Molecules, Molecules 30(18):3713 (2025) - second, independent matrix-isolation procedure (ARS-2HW closed-cycle helium cryostat, CsI window at 15 K, spectra at 10 K)

reported_equipment: closed-cycle helium cryostat with a DE-202 A expander

requirements.rationale: The matrix is deposited and held with the optical substrate at 15 K; the machine must be able to reach and hold that sample temperature.
Argon matrix isolation needs a base temperature of 15 K or lower; a machine whose lowest temperature is above 15 K cannot form a rigid Ar matrix.
Deposition and spectroscopy happen inside an evacuated chamber; an atmospheric-pressure cold space would frost the window and destroy the matrix.
The reported working vacuum of the matrix chamber is about 3.5e-5 mbar; poorer vacuum deposits residual water and air with the matrix gas.
The IR beam and the UV photolysis beam must reach the cold deposit, so the cold space needs optical windows; the sample itself sits on a cold optical substrate.
Spectra are taken over 4000-400 cm-1, i.e. 2500-25000 nm, so the cryostat windows must transmit the whole mid-infrared (hence CsI rather than glass or quartz).

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
